meta.name: security-audit map
meta.tagline: Cloudflare's security-audit skill, step by step: recon, coverage-led hunting, adversarial validation, schema-checked findings, fresh-eyes verification, then reports.

labels.stageNote: **This is a phase, not a skill.** The parent agent runs the parts inside it, in order.
labels.anyNote: **Not tied to one phase.** These modes, rails and blocks apply across the run.

sources.label: Cloudflare blog: Build your own vulnerability harness

stages.name: Reconnaissance
stages.principle: Map the target **from source only**, then turn it into a ==deterministic coverage ledger==: the list of everything that must be checked.
when: When you ask for a full audit → setup and the budget gate run first
When prior runs exist → they are read so this run targets the gaps
When the four recon agents report → the parent writes architecture.md and the ledger

stages.name: Hunting
stages.principle: Isolated hunters work **from the ledger, unit by unit**, and critics look for gaps after every wave. ==No unit is silently skipped==.
when: When units are planned → rank them and brief one hunter per group
When a wave ends → a fresh critic proposes missing or reopened units
When two critic passes come back clean → hunting ends

stages.name: Validation
stages.principle: Every unique candidate goes to a **fresh verifier that did not find it** and tries to ==disprove it==.
when: When hunting ends → merge candidates by fingerprint
When a candidate is unique → one fresh general verifier
When it decides → confirmed, needs_validation or rejected

stages.name: Structured output
stages.principle: All final records go into **findings.json**, checked against a JSON schema. ==JSON first, prose later==.
when: When verifiers have decided → write findings.json sorted by fingerprint
Before moving on → both validators must pass

stages.name: Verification
stages.principle: **Fresh agents re-check the final records** themselves. A material change gets ==yet another independent verifier==.
when: When findings.json validates → one fresh research verifier per confirmed and needs_validation record
When a replacement changes meaning → a brand-new verifier checks it
When everything has passed → the run can be marked complete

stages.name: Reporting
stages.principle: Reports are **derived from the verified records and the ledger**, ==written last==, with no live-probe instructions.
when: Only after Phase 5 passes → write REPORT.md, FINDINGS-DETAIL.md and NEEDS-VALIDATION.md

categories.name: Set up the run
categories.blurb: Write the run facts, then check the budget can pay.
categories.principle: Nothing launches until the run is **written down** and ==the budget covers the minimum==.
when: When full audit mode starts → run-metadata first
When a budget is set → budget-gate before any agent
categories.chainWhy: RECONNAISSANCE.md:5 says the parent initializes run-metadata.json, applies the pre-reconnaissance budget gate, then creates scratch roots and the ledger.

categories.name: Map the target (4 agents)
categories.blurb: Four read-only research agents, launched together.
categories.principle: Four **read-only `research` agents** run ==in parallel== and return facts; they write no files.
when: When recon starts → all four launch together
When a deployment mode or subsystem is not covered → add a focused recon agent (if the budget allows)
categories.chainWhy: RECONNAISSANCE.md:7 says to launch several research agents in parallel. No arrows: none waits for another.

categories.name: Plan the coverage
categories.blurb: Reuse prior runs, summarize, seed and validate the ledger.
categories.principle: Turn the facts into **work units** and ==validate them before anyone hunts==.
when: When prior runs exist → prior-runs first
When the summary is done → seed the ledger, then run the validator
categories.chainWhy: SKILL.md:96 reads prior runs before planning; RECONNAISSANCE.md:73-156 writes architecture.md, then the ledger, and runs the validator after seeding.

categories.name: Assign the work
categories.blurb: Rank units, then build each hunter's brief.
categories.principle: **Highest-risk units first**, and every brief ==copies the blocks verbatim==.
when: When hunters are capped → rank-units decides the order
When a unit is assigned → build its hunter-prompt
categories.chainWhy: HUNTING.md:7-9 ranks and marks units in_progress before launch; HUNTING.md:11-23 then defines the prompt parts.

categories.name: Hunt
categories.blurb: One isolated hunter per unit group, one JSON result.
categories.principle: Hunters **read deep, run little**, and return ==structured results the parent can dedupe==.
when: When a unit is in progress → a hunter owns it
When it finishes → hunter-result updates the ledger
categories.chainWhy: HUNTING.md:27-97 is the method; HUNTING.md:168-219 is the result contract and the parent's ledger update.

categories.name: Find the gaps
categories.blurb: Critic after each wave, then a final-clean critic.
categories.principle: Coverage is complete only when ==two critic passes in a row find nothing== (standard and deep).
when: After every wave → post-wave-critic
When it is clean and nothing is planned → final-clean-critic
categories.chainWhy: HUNTING.md:223 runs a critic immediately after each wave; HUNTING.md:247 spends the separate final-clean reserve only after a clean pass.

categories.name: Try to disprove it
categories.blurb: Merge, verify independently, pick the verdict.
categories.principle: **The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.** ==Adversarial by design==.
when: When hunting ends → consolidate
For each unique candidate → candidate-verifier
When it decides → verdict-rules
categories.chainWhy: VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md:5 consolidates first, then gives each unique candidate to a fresh verifier; L87 sets the verdict rules.

categories.name: Write and validate
categories.principle: The schema uses `additionalProperties: false`, so ==the JSON stays exact==.
when: When decisions are in → findings.json
Right after → validate-findings plus the ledger validator
categories.chainWhy: VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md:97-116 writes the file, then runs both validators.

categories.name: Three verdicts
categories.blurb: Each record is exactly one of these.
categories.principle: Three **separate contracts**: ==only confirmed gets a severity==.
when: When proven → confirmed-record
When one outside fact is missing → needs-validation-record
When disproved → rejected-record
categories.chainWhy: These are the three oneOf branches of report-schema.json; a record is one of them, not a step in a sequence.

categories.name: Re-check the records
categories.blurb: Fresh verifier per record; another for big changes.
categories.principle: **Never skip independent review of a confirmed record**, ==in any profile==.
when: For each final record → record-verifier
When a replacement is material → fresh-re-verifier
categories.chainWhy: VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md:122 launches the record verifiers; L145 sends material replacements to a new independent verifier.

categories.name: Finish line
categories.principle: Two terminal states only. ==Gaps are disclosed, not hidden==.
when: When all records pass → complete
When a budget or critic ran out → incomplete + reason
categories.chainWhy: SKILL.md:179 names exactly two terminal states.

categories.name: Write the reports
categories.blurb: Three files, all derived from the final records.
categories.principle: **Prose comes last** and ==never changes a verdict, severity or blocker==.
when: Only after Phase 5 passes → all three reports
categories.chainWhy: VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md:153 derives all three from the same final records and ledger; none depends on another.

anytime.name: Pick the mode
anytime.blurb: Guidance by default; the full workflow only when you explicitly ask for an audit.

anytime.name: Run size
anytime.blurb: Profiles change breadth and redundancy, never the evidence bar.

anytime.name: Safety rails
anytime.blurb: Where code may run, who may write, how evidence is copied, and how spend is reserved.

anytime.name: Proof and severity rules
anytime.blurb: What counts as a finding, how it is scored and fixed, and what the skill refuses to do.

anytime.name: Attack classes: core
anytime.blurb: Ordinary attack-class blocks from ATTACK-CLASSES.md, picked per unit in Phase 1.

anytime.name: Attack classes: wider net
anytime.blurb: Design abuse, chains, a no-category hunter and a literal basics check.

anytime.name: Companions: code and protocols
anytime.blurb: Domain files selected when recon finds the matching boundary.

anytime.name: Companions: platform and data
anytime.blurb: Domain files selected when recon finds the matching boundary.

run-metadata.name: run-metadata.json
when: When **full audit mode** starts → the parent resolves the run values and writes [[run-metadata]] first
When you did not name an output folder → it uses ==`~/security-audit-skill/<repo>/run-<N>`==
run-metadata.whatItIs: The **run's fact sheet**. The parent agent writes it ==before it hands work to any other agent==.
howItWorks: The parent resolves the **skill folder, target repo, repo name, output folder and source ref** (commit, and whether the tree is dirty)
The output folder sits **outside the target**. Inside it only if you pick it and Git ignores it
It writes `run_id`, `target`, `profile`, `scope_paths`, `budget`, companion files, prior-run paths and ==`run_status: "in_progress"`==
It is updated only when those facts change. Candidate state lives in the ledger and `findings.json`
behindTheScenes: only writer of shared run files

budget-gate.name: budget-gate
when: When you set a **budget** (or the parent proposes one for a big target) → the gate runs before any recon agent
When the budget **cannot fund the minimum** → no agent launches and the run is marked incomplete
budget-gate.whatItIs: A **spend check before any agent starts**. A budget is counted as ==a maximum number of agent calls== across all phases.
howItWorks: It reserves the **four baseline recon calls**
It reserves the **critics**: one final critic for `quick`, a post-wave plus a separate final-clean critic for `standard` and `deep`
It reserves **at least one verifier** call
Too small? It asks for a bigger budget or a narrower scope. Unchanged, it records ==`incomplete_reason: budget_cannot_fund_reconnaissance_and_reserves`==

agent-1a-stack.name: agent-1a-stack
when: When recon starts → [[agent-1a-stack]] runs **in parallel** with the other three recon agents
agent-1a-stack.whatItIs: A read-only **`research` agent** that learns ==what the product is and how it builds==, with no network.
howItWorks: Product type, users, operators and **trust-sensitive actions**
Languages, frameworks, build system, runtimes and **deployment models** it can see
Entry points and subsystem boundaries, with `file:line` refs
Offline **build and test commands** (listed, ==not run== during recon), a comparable product if one is source-grounded, and missing toolchains

agent-1b-trust.name: agent-1b-trust
when: When recon starts → [[agent-1b-trust]] maps who may do what, alongside the other recon agents
agent-1b-trust.whatItIs: A read-only **`research` agent** that maps ==every principal, permission and control==.
howItWorks: Each **lower-trust principal** and the actions it has by design
Authentication at each entry, **per-resource authorization** and tenant or owner scope
Process, CI, plugin, model/tool, device or local-IPC **authority**, plus privilege changes, revocation and fallback paths
Which controls are **visible in source** and which depend on ==a deployment fact it cannot see==

agent-1c-inputs.name: agent-1c-inputs
when: When recon starts → [[agent-1c-inputs]] inventories every way input gets in
agent-1c-inputs.whatItIs: A read-only **`research` agent** that lists ==every place outside input enters== and follows it to the dangerous spots.
howItWorks: Covers HTTP/browser, RPC/messages, files and archives, CLI/env/config, plugins/CI, cloud events, **model context and tool arguments**, mobile/deep links and local IPC
Follows **transformations, stored copies and security-relevant sinks** for each surface
Records limits and **parallel paths to the same effect**
Returns paths and line numbers. It ==does not execute or send inputs==

agent-1d-sandbox.name: agent-1d-sandbox
when: When recon starts → [[agent-1d-sandbox]] decides what can be safely run later
agent-1d-sandbox.whatItIs: A read-only **`research` agent** that works out ==what may be executed, and what must never be==.
howItWorks: Small **offline tests and fixtures** that could check a trust boundary with dummy data
Commands that would **fetch dependencies, publish, call paid APIs or touch shared state**: marked prohibited
Deployed controls that source cannot prove → **needs_validation** if decisive
Whether the machine can enforce the **sandbox** (no network, empty env, read-only target, scratch-only writes, limits) and safe artifact promotion. ==Missing controls block execution==

prior-runs.name: prior-runs
when: When **earlier runs exist** for the same repo → the parent reads every prior ledger and `findings.json` before planning
When there is no prior ledger → the final report says so
prior-runs.whatItIs: How runs **add up**. Each new run ==targets the gaps the last runs left==, and nothing old counts as covered by default.
howItWorks: Compares each prior record and unit with the **current source**. A matching commit alone is not proof
An unchanged prior **confirmed** record is carried in with the same fingerprint, excluded from hunters, and **re-verified**
Changed source becomes a **revalidation unit**. Prior needs-validation, deferred, blocked and out-of-scope work becomes current work
A prior rejection suppresses only ==that exact unchanged claim==, not the coverage unit

architecture-md.name: architecture.md
when: When the recon agents report back → the parent writes [[architecture-md]]
When a domain boundary is found → the matching **companion file** is selected here
architecture-md.whatItIs: The parent's **~1,000-word summary** of the target. Every hunter gets it ==verbatim== in its prompt.
howItWorks: Product, principals, normal authority and **protected resources**
A **comparable-software baseline** when one is source-grounded, used to calibrate, never to dismiss a finding
Stack, entry surfaces, **source-to-sink paths**, trust boundaries and the strongest control on each
Prior-run gaps, and ==which companion files apply and why==. A file is chosen for a boundary, not because a dependency name appears

coverage-ledger.name: coverage-ledger.json
when: When `architecture.md` is done → the parent seeds [[coverage-ledger]]
After **every agent result** → the parent alone updates it
coverage-ledger.whatItIs: The **coverage claim** itself. One unit per ==entry surface × trust boundary × subsystem × attack class==.
howItWorks: Each unit has **stable canonical refs** and a `coverage_id` built from them (percent-encoded, joined with `::`), never from line numbers or agent names
Each unit lists starting paths, its **attack-class block**, selected and excluded companion blocks with reasons
States follow a strict table: `planned`, `in_progress`, `covered`, `candidate`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `not_applicable`, `out_of_scope`
A summary or an agent count is **not coverage evidence**. ==Only paths and checks in a structured result close a unit==

validate-ledger.name: validate-coverage-ledger
when: After **seeding**, after **every parent update**, and **before Phase 6** → run [[validate-ledger]]
When it reports errors → fix every one before assigning work
validate-ledger.whatItIs: A **zero-dependency Node validator** for `coverage-ledger.json`. ==An invalid ledger cannot drive another assignment==.
howItWorks: Checks required fields, the **state table**, canonical lowercase agent IDs and coverage-ID derivation
Rejects duplicate IDs and **one tuple written with different refs**
Caps input at **5 MiB**, 64 nesting levels and 10,000 units, and reports at most 100 errors

rank-units.name: rank-units
when: When a budget or profile **caps the hunter count** → units are taken in this order
When a unit cannot be reached → it is marked `deferred` with a reason, never silently dropped
rank-units.whatItIs: The **priority order** for planned units. Ties break by `coverage_id` so ==runs stay deterministic==.
howItWorks: **Unauthenticated** or lowest-trust entry surfaces first
Boundaries guarding the **most valuable resources**: credentials, cross-tenant data, code execution, release authority
**Prior-run gaps**, revalidation targets and changed source before same-source re-passes
Classes that ==historically yield confirmed findings== for this kind of target

hunter-prompt.name: hunter-prompt
when: When a unit is assigned → the parent builds one [[hunter-prompt]] per hunter
hunter-prompt.whatItIs: The **exact brief** every hunter gets. Blocks are ==copied verbatim, never named==.
howItWorks: Role preamble, then `architecture.md` **verbatim**, then the assigned coverage IDs and paths
The selected **attack-class block** plus each companion's Core discipline, chosen classes, Universal moves and Validation rules
**Excluded blocks** with reasons, the core hunting method, the promotion procedure and the candidate gate
Carried prior exclusions, peer-owned IDs not to duplicate, scratch paths and the ==structured-result contract==

hunter.name: hunter
when: When a unit is `in_progress` → one isolated [[hunter]] owns it
When it spots a different boundary → it returns it as `uncovered` instead of chasing it
hunter.whatItIs: An isolated **`general` agent** that reads code ==at depth== to find a broken security rule in its own units.
howItWorks: Follows each input through **parsing, identity, authorization, state, copies and the final sink**, including retry, legacy and error paths
Works from a **concrete invariant**: lower-trust principal, accepted value, the control that should stop it, the path after it, the smallest effect, the fix
Tests **sad paths**: empty, negative, duplicate, stale, revoked, reordered, concurrent, mid-migration
Runs only the **narrowest local check**, inside the sandbox, and ==stops at the minimum effect==

hunter-result.name: hunter-result
when: When a hunter finishes → it returns exactly one JSON object, no prose
When the parent receives it → it updates only the matching ledger units
hunter-result.whatItIs: The hunter's **structured report**: ==every assigned unit appears exactly once==.
howItWorks: `units`: each with a disposition `covered`, `candidate` or `blocked`, reviewed paths and **checks**
`candidates`: schema-shaped records with `proposed_verdict` confirmed or needs_validation, passed through the **candidate gate**
`hardening`: non-finding notes kept for the report. `uncovered`: new boundaries for a new unit
The parent **dedupes by fingerprint, then root cause**. A malformed result leaves the unit `planned`

post-wave-critic.name: post-wave-critic
when: Right **after every hunter wave** → one fresh critic runs, paid from the reserve
post-wave-critic.whatItIs: A fresh read-only **`research` agent** that proposes ==coverage, not findings==.
howItWorks: Gets `architecture.md`, the **full ledger** and current candidate fingerprints
Looks for unmapped entry points, unchecked parallel paths, missing lifecycle modes, **unjustified exclusions** and units closed without checks
Returns `missing_units`, `reassign_ids`, `resolved_prior_leads` and `stop`
Reopened units keep their old attempt in `attempts`; the ==next hunter is always a fresh owner==

final-clean-critic.name: final-clean-critic
when: In `standard` and `deep` → when the post-wave critic finds no work and nothing is planned
In `quick` → there is no second critic; leftover work is marked `deferred`
final-clean-critic.whatItIs: A **separate, reserved critic**. Coverage counts as complete ==only when this one also finds nothing==.
howItWorks: Runs only after a clean post-wave pass with **no planned units left**
If it finds work, the loop repeats: **wave → post-wave critic → final-clean critic**
An early stop marks untouched units `deferred` and the gap is disclosed
A silent wave or agent cap is ==never evidence of complete coverage==

consolidate.name: consolidate
when: After the clean critic pass (or a recorded early stop) → the parent merges all candidates
consolidate.whatItIs: The parent **merges candidates by fingerprint and root cause**, so ==each real issue is checked once==.
howItWorks: Merges Phase 2 candidates and **carried prior confirmations**
One root cause with several entry paths is **one candidate** with the strongest trace
Related but independent missing controls keep **separate fingerprints**

candidate-verifier.name: candidate-verifier
when: For **every unique candidate** → a fresh `general` verifier that did not hunt it
candidate-verifier.whatItIs: An independent agent told: =="You did not write this candidate. Try to refute it."==
howItWorks: Gets only the candidate, its unit checks, needed architecture facts, the companion validation blocks and the schema. **Never another verifier's conclusion**
**Re-reads every cited line** and confirms the first trace step is a real lower-trust entry
Rebuilds the strongest controls on the path and **independently reproduces** the minimum result in the sandbox when it can
Checks likelihood, impact, confidence and fix match only the evidence, then returns one JSON `decision` + `record`

verdict-rules.name: verdict-rules
when: When a verifier decides → these rules pick the verdict
verdict-rules.whatItIs: Three **distinct outcomes**. `needs_validation` is ==never a parking place for a speculative idea==.
howItWorks: **Confirmed** only after the full path and a bounded observed result are independently established
**Needs validation** when one specific deployment or runtime fact is still unknown
**Rejected** when source, local behavior, a visible control, no real impact or an impossible prerequisite refutes it
A malformed verifier answer is discarded and re-run; if the budget runs out, the candidate stays in the ledger only

findings-json.name: findings.json
when: After Phase 3 → the parent writes all independently decided records, **sorted by fingerprint**
findings-json.whatItIs: The **machine-readable result**. The reports are derived from it, ==never the other way round==.
howItWorks: Holds `confirmed`, `needs_validation` and `rejected` records
The parent reads `report-schema.json` **right before writing**; `additionalProperties: false`, so no hunter wrapper fields
Each record has a stable fingerprint, title, description and **repository-relative** source paths
Traces start at `entrypoint`, end at `sink`, with `propagation` between

validate-findings.name: validate-findings
when: In **Phase 4**, and again after **every Phase 5 replacement** → run it together with the ledger validator
validate-findings.whatItIs: A **zero-dependency Node validator** for `findings.json` against `report-schema.json`. ==Passing proves format, not truth==.
howItWorks: Interprets the schema directly and adds checks like **duplicate and unsorted fingerprints** and safe repo-relative paths
Rejects input over **5 MiB**, 1,000 findings or 64 nesting levels
Runs next to `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs`; fix every error before continuing

confirmed-record.name: confirmed-record
when: When the trace is complete **and** a bounded local result was observed → [[confirmed-record]]
confirmed-record.whatItIs: A **proven vulnerability**. The only verdict that ==gets a severity==.
howItWorks: Fields: `root_cause`, `intended_behavior`, `trace`, `evidence`, `conditions`, `execution`, `remediation`, `severity`, `confidence`
`execution` is **target-neutral**: an HTTP input, CLI call, library call, fixture or rendered policy, whatever the target natively uses
Severity is likelihood × impact, and **overall cannot exceed the demonstrated impact**

needs-validation-record.name: needs_validation
when: When a source-grounded lead hits **one fact outside source** (deployment, provider, identity) → [[needs-validation-record]]
needs-validation-record.whatItIs: A **specific, blocked hypothesis**, not a low-confidence finding. It ==never gets a severity==.
howItWorks: Fields: `claimed_root_cause`, `trace`, `evidence`, nonempty `blockers` and a `validation_plan`
The plan has a bounded **`local`** step, an owner-observed **`deployment`** check, or both when both resolve distinct facts
A deployment check asks the owner to look. It is ==never audit traffic sent to a live system==

rejected-record.name: rejected-record
when: When validation **disproves** a candidate → [[rejected-record]]
rejected-record.whatItIs: A **disproved claim kept on record**, so ==future runs do not repeat it== without new evidence.
howItWorks: Fields: `claimed_root_cause`, `trace`, `evidence` and `reason`
No severity, execution, remediation, blockers or plan
Never described as a finding; mentioned only to explain a **prior disagreement or coverage decision**
behindTheScenes: next run skips the unchanged claim

record-verifier.name: record-verifier
when: For **every final confirmed and needs_validation record** → one fresh `research` verifier, all in parallel
In a `quick` run → Phase 3 and Phase 5 merge into one fresh reviewer per candidate
record-verifier.whatItIs: A second, independent check of ==the structured record itself==, not the hunter's write-up.
howItWorks: For **confirmed**: every path and line, the real entry interface, every condition and preventing layer, impact, severity split and the fix
For **needs_validation**: the path is real, every blocker is decisive, the plan is exact, the fingerprint matches
Returns `{"decision":"verified", "fingerprint": …}` or `{"decision":"replace", "record": …}`
Both kinds are checked: ==a misleading needs_validation handoff wastes owner time==

fresh-re-verifier.name: fresh-re-verifier
when: When a Phase 5 replacement **promotes a verdict** or materially changes root cause, trace, input, result, impact or severity
fresh-re-verifier.whatItIs: Another **brand-new verifier** that did not hunt, validate or propose the change. ==A material change is never applied unchecked==.
howItWorks: Re-checks current source and **independently reproduces** any decisive local result
Returns `verified` or another replacement; repeat with a fresh verifier each time
No budget or independence left? The record is **removed**, its unit stays an unresolved candidate, and the run is `incomplete`
Small wording or line-number fixes are applied directly, then **both validators run again**

run-status.name: run-status
when: When every ledger candidate has a final disposition and every record passed Phase 5 → `complete`
When budget, validation or a critic ran out → `incomplete` with an exact reason
run-status.whatItIs: The run ends in ==exactly one of two terminal states==. It never stops mid-phase.
howItWorks: **(a)** All Phase 6 files are written and **both validators pass**
**(b)** `run_status: "incomplete"` is recorded with its exact reason, e.g. `validation_budget_exhausted` or `critic_budget_exhausted`, and the gap is disclosed in the report
A user-set strict budget is **never exceeded silently**

report-md.name: REPORT.md
when: Only **after Phase 5 passes** for every retained record → the parent writes [[report-md]]
report-md.whatItIs: The **owner-facing report**, derived from the final records and the ledger. ==Prose never changes a verdict or severity==.
howItWorks: Run profile, scope, budget spent vs planned, source ref, **sandboxed source-and-local-only** statement, prior-run use, and deferred or out-of-scope coverage
A short **posture summary** and a confirmed-findings table: severity, title, boundary, one-line result
Each confirmed finding with **bounded reproduction**, impact, priority and the smallest source fix, then a separate NEEDS VALIDATION table
Hardening notes, positive patterns and a **coverage summary**. A clean run can have ==zero findings== and says so

findings-detail-md.name: FINDINGS-DETAIL.md
when: For each **confirmed `medium`, `high` or `critical`** record → a full detail entry
findings-detail-md.whatItIs: The **full reproduction file** for serious findings, written ==in the target's own interface==.
howItWorks: Ordered trace and evidence, the **dummy attacker** and the affected dummy resource
The native input, invocation or fixture, with exact **bounded** instructions and the observed output
Conditions, containment, the **source-level fix** and a regression case

needs-validation-md.name: NEEDS-VALIDATION.md
when: For **every unresolved record** → one entry the owner can act on
needs-validation-md.whatItIs: The **open-leads file**: prioritized, ==with no severity== and no live test guidance.
howItWorks: Source trace, verified evidence, the **exact blocker** and the affected boundary
Each applicable **bounded local** or **owner-observed** resolution plan
Never assumes the missing deployment fact

guidance-mode.name: guidance-mode
when: When you ask a **security question**, a focused review or triage of one finding → [[guidance-mode]]
When a request could mean either mode → it asks **one focused question** first
guidance-mode.whatItIs: The **default mode**. Loading the skill ==does not authorize the full audit or any file writes==.
howItWorks: Uses only the **relevant parts** of the skill
Does **not** run all six phases, create an output folder or write audit artifacts
May launch focused agents; their results go back to your current task
The execution-safety rules still apply

example.situation: you want a second opinion on one auth check.
example.youType: is this JWT check in src/auth.ts safe?
whatHappens: It reads only the relevant code.
It may launch a focused agent.
example.youGet: **An answer in the chat**, no audit folder.

full-audit-mode.name: full-audit-mode
when: When you **explicitly** ask to audit or pen-test a codebase, ask for a full/comprehensive/end-to-end review, or ask for report files → [[full-audit-mode]]
full-audit-mode.whatItIs: The **complete workflow**: ==all six phases, in order==, writing the run files to the output folder.
howItWorks: Resolves setup, writes `run-metadata.json` and runs the **budget gate**
Runs **Reconnaissance → Hunting → Validation → Structured output → Record verification → Report**
Ends only when every Phase 6 file is written and **both validators pass**, or the run is recorded `incomplete`

example.situation: you want a real audit of a repo before launch.
whatHappens: Fresh verifiers try to disprove every candidate.
example.youGet: **REPORT.md, FINDINGS-DETAIL.md, NEEDS-VALIDATION.md** plus `findings.json` and the ledger.

quick-profile.name: quick-profile
when: When the target is **small**, it is a **re-run**, or you want a fast first look → [[quick-profile]]
quick-profile.whatItIs: A **bounded pass**. It always reports itself as ==partial coverage==.
howItWorks: Coarser units: surface × boundary × attack class, one all-in-scope subsystem
**Exactly one hunter wave** and one final critic; no follow-up wave
One fresh verifier per candidate does both Phase 3 and Phase 5

standard-profile.name: standard-profile
when: When nothing else is asked for → [[standard-profile]]
standard-profile.whatItIs: **The workflow as written.** ==This is the default profile==.
howItWorks: Critic waves until a post-wave pass and a separate final-clean pass both find nothing
Candidate validation and record verification stay **separate fresh agents**

deep-profile.name: deep-profile
when: When the target is **high-stakes or large** → [[deep-profile]]
deep-profile.whatItIs: The **most redundant** profile. Profiles change breadth, ==never the evidence bar==.
howItWorks: Units split per **subsystem and lifecycle mode**
Critic waves to a clean pass, separate validation and verification agents
Prior same-source covered units get an **independent second pass**

scoped-run.name: scoped-run
when: When you name **paths, one subsystem, one companion domain, or a diff** between two refs → [[scoped-run]]
scoped-run.whatItIs: An audit of **a subset**. Everything else is recorded `out_of_scope`, ==never `covered`==.
howItWorks: Seeds units only for in-scope surfaces
Critics still note out-of-scope gaps, recorded as `out_of_scope` for later runs
Presents itself as **partial coverage**

os-sandbox.name: os-sandbox
when: Whenever the target's own builds, tests, browsers, fuzzers or fixtures would run → only inside [[os-sandbox]]
When any control is missing → it **does not run** target code
os-sandbox.whatItIs: The **execution boundary**. Source reading is read-only; target code runs ==only in an OS-enforced sandbox==.
howItWorks: **No external network**; an isolated loopback only for a local fixture
An **empty environment** from an allowlist, scratch-local `HOME`, temp and caches
**Read-only target and toolchain**; writes only to the agent's `scratch/`
Low CPU, memory, process, file-size, disk and wall-clock **limits**. No installs, no live endpoints, no real credentials
behindTheScenes: sandbox (no net, empty env, read-only, limits)

write-isolation.name: write-isolation
when: Throughout a full audit → the **parent is the only writer** of shared run files
write-isolation.whatItIs: Who may write where. ==Agents never touch shared files, target source or each other's folders==.
howItWorks: The parent alone writes `run-metadata.json`, `architecture.md`, `coverage-ledger.json`, `findings.json` and the three reports
Each hunter or verifier gets `agents/<agent-id>/` with **`scratch/`** and parent-owned **`artifacts/`**
Agent IDs are **lowercase** and never a Windows device name; `/tmp` and home are never a fallback

artifact-promotion.name: artifact-promotion
when: After the sandbox and **all its processes end** → trusted parent-side code promotes allowlisted files
artifact-promotion.whatItIs: An **11-step race-safe copy** from scratch to artifacts. Only promoted files ==count as local evidence==.
howItWorks: Allowlist and **byte limits** set before execution; descriptors are never passed to the sandbox
No-follow, directory-relative walks; `fstat` checks for a **regular file with one link** and the size limit
Never globs scratch, extracts archives, or promotes symlinks, FIFOs, sockets, devices or hard links
Any failed check discards the entry; decisive evidence becomes a **needs_validation** blocker

cost-budget.name: cost-budget
when: When a **budget** is set → hunters are funded only after critics and validation are reserved
cost-budget.whatItIs: The ledger makes spend countable: ==one unit ≈ one hunter, one candidate ≈ one or two verifiers==.
howItWorks: Count recon, every critic and the final-clean critic as agent calls
**Reserve critics and validation before hunting** (about 30% of the balance when unsure)
Assign hunters by priority until the hunting allowance is spent
Before each later wave, reserve its critic again; if it does not fit, the wave's units become `deferred`

boundary-and-result.name: boundary-and-result
when: For **every candidate** → name the boundary and the concrete result first
boundary-and-result.whatItIs: The first rule: a finding needs ==a real trust boundary and a concrete result==.
howItWorks: Name the **lower-trust principal**, the accepted input, the intended control and the crossed boundary
Name the **affected principal or resource** and the observed result
A missing best practice, guessed deployment behavior, generic crash or **self-impact** is not a finding
Defense-in-depth gaps are **hardening notes**: if Layer A stops the attack, missing Layer B is not a vulnerability

sources.label: SKILL.md require a boundary and result (L138-140)

severity-anchors.name: severity-anchors
when: When a **confirmed** record is scored → use these anchors
severity-anchors.whatItIs: Severity is **likelihood × impact** of what was shown. ==It cannot exceed the demonstrated impact==.
howItWorks: **Critical**: an unauthenticated actor gets code execution, full data-store access or arbitrary account takeover
**High**: an explicit control is fully defeated (auth bypass, cross-tenant read/write, stored script, authenticated RCE)
**Medium**: a real violation with limited blast radius. **Low**: non-secret internals. **Informational**: minimal impact
High vs medium: does it **fully defeat** a control, or only weaken it?

smallest-fix.name: smallest-fix
smallest-fix.trigger: fix at the last trusted check
when: For **each confirmed finding** → describe the narrowest source change
smallest-fix.whatItIs: The audit **describes fixes, it never edits the target**. Prefer ==specific repo-relative changes plus a regression test==.
howItWorks: Name the **invariant** the code must enforce
Change it at the **last trusted decision point**
Avoid generic hardening advice

anti-patterns.name: anti-patterns
when: When reviewing any output → check it against the 10 anti-patterns
anti-patterns.whatItIs: The **ten mistakes** the skill is built to avoid. ==Checklist deviations are not vulnerabilities==.
howItWorks: No **defense-in-depth advice** without a reachable violation, no live or shared-environment testing
No **guessing** provider, proxy, browser, identity or deployment behavior; no self-impact as cross-boundary
No **prose-only** hunter results, no re-reporting carried priors, no severity on needs_validation
**Never write the report before independent verification**, and never let prose and JSON disagree

ac-injection.name: injection
when: When Phase 1 finds a matching boundary → a ledger unit points at this block and a hunter gets it **verbatim**
ac-injection.whatItIs: Traces **untrusted input to a dangerous sink**: SQL, HTML, shell, templates, file paths, redirects, deserialization.
howItWorks: Looks for **indirect injection**: data stored safely, then used dangerously by other code
Checks field names, keys, headers and metadata, **not just values**
Includes secondary systems: logs, caches, search indexes, analytics

ac-access-control.name: access-control
when: When Phase 1 finds a matching boundary → a ledger unit points at this block and a hunter gets it **verbatim**
ac-access-control.whatItIs: Verifies a caller **cannot act outside its authority**: the ==right permission, for the right resource, by the right mechanism==.
howItWorks: A weaker path to the same state change? A body field that **overrides** the permission?
Authentication without **authorization**? Several access paths with inconsistent checks?
Do **bulk, batch, export and import** enforce per-item permissions?

ac-resource-file.name: resource-and-file
when: When Phase 1 finds a matching boundary → a ledger unit points at this block and a hunter gets it **verbatim**
ac-resource-file.whatItIs: **Resource and file handling**: path traversal, SSRF, unsafe deserialization, zip slip, temp files.
howItWorks: Traversal through **symlinks, encoded sequences and null bytes**
SSRF through redirects, DNS rebinding and **URL parser differentials**
File **TOCTOU** races; memory safety where it applies

ac-crypto.name: crypto-and-secrets
when: When Phase 1 finds a matching boundary → a ledger unit points at this block and a hunter gets it **verbatim**
ac-crypto.whatItIs: **Cryptography and secrets**: weak randomness, hardcoded or leaked secrets, broken primitives.
howItWorks: Weak randomness for **tokens, keys and nonces**
Missing HMAC checks, nonce reuse, **timing side-channels** on secret comparison
Does a crypto **error path fall back** to no crypto?

ac-business-logic.name: business-logic
when: When Phase 1 finds a matching boundary → a ledger unit points at this block and a hunter gets it **verbatim**
ac-business-logic.whatItIs: **Business logic** flaws that scanners cannot find and that ==yield high-impact findings==.
howItWorks: **State machine** skips, replays and partial-failure rollbacks; check-then-act **races**
Negative, zero or overflowing **quantities**; the right check for the business rule
Implicit trust in stored data, **time boundaries**, and the posture when config or a dependency is missing

ac-feature-abuse.name: feature-abuse
when: When Phase 1 finds a matching boundary → a ledger unit points at this block and a hunter gets it **verbatim**
ac-feature-abuse.whatItIs: **Feature abuse and data leakage**: legitimate features used for unintended purposes.
howItWorks: **Export or backup** as exfiltration; **import or restore** as injection
Search, filter and sort as an **oracle**; enumeration through errors, timing or sizes
Preview and draft leaks; **webhook or notification URLs** as SSRF

ac-chained.name: chained-trust
when: When Phase 1 finds a matching boundary → a ledger unit points at this block and a hunter gets it **verbatim**
ac-chained.whatItIs: **Chained vulnerabilities and trust boundaries**: allowed behavior that breaks when another part relies on a stronger guarantee.
howItWorks: **Multi-step** failures, confirming each prerequisite
What component A guarantees vs what **component B assumes**; second-order use of stored data
Scope growth after delegation or refresh; **timing windows**; rollback and restore

ac-wildcard.name: wildcard
when: When Phase 1 finds a matching boundary → a ledger unit points at this block and a hunter gets it **verbatim**
ac-wildcard.whatItIs: The **wildcard** hunter gets ==no category== and looks outside the standard classes.
howItWorks: The **strangest** code, half-finished or experimental features, hidden endpoints
API calls the frontend never makes; features **mixed** that were not designed together
Git history (reverted fixes, removed secrets) and **what the tests do not test**

ac-obvious.name: obvious-things
when: When Phase 1 finds a matching boundary → a ledger unit points at this block and a hunter gets it **verbatim**
ac-obvious.whatItIs: The **obvious things** hunter checks basic exposures literally. It needs to be thorough, ==not creative==.
howItWorks: Hardcoded secrets, security **TODO/FIXME**s, debug mode, seed credentials, unprotected `/debug` or `/admin`
Checked-in `.env` or keys, `.gitignore` gaps, **unpinned or CVE dependencies**, dynamic `eval`
Permissive **CORS**, cookie flags, open redirects, TLS, stack traces. A flag is not a finding until the impact is traced
